questions.0.explain.t: RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) gives the model external context at query time.

questions.0.options.1.t: Training a model from scratch on your data

questions.1.explain.t: Retrieved content is untrusted input: it can carry instructions that the model obeys.

questions.1.options.0.t: Malicious instructions hidden in retrieved documents (indirect prompt injection)

questions.1.options.1.t: The model running out of RAM

questions.1.options.3.t: Lack of HTTPS in the tokenizer

questions.1.q.t: Which security risk is typical of RAG?

questions.2.explain.t: With real passages in the context, the model depends less on parametric memory.

questions.2.options.0.t: Because it anchors the answer in retrieved sources, which can be cited

questions.2.options.1.t: Because it makes the model bigger

questions.2.q.t: Why does RAG help reduce hallucination?
